messages:
alex: Heads-up — deploybot just flagged the v0.48.1 release during the pre-canary checks. It failed the dependency-integrity check in the SBOM step, holding the pipeline.

deploy-bot: Automated check failed: SBOM integrity mismatch for artifact:redwood/runtime:0.48.1
-- expected digest: sha256:aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66aa77bb88cc99ddeeff00112233445566778899aa
-- found digest:    sha256:aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66aa77bb88cc99ddeeff00112233445566778899bb
Action: canary blocked; open ticket created: https://issues.internal/RI-4672

maria: ack. how big is the delta? is this likely a signing issue or a tampered layer?

alex: quick diff of layers looks like a single package layer changed (pip wheels). vuln-scan shows 1 medium sev CVE (CVE-2025-1234) introduced in that wheel — depends on packaging version.

irene: tagging security-oncall. need more context: which package, and is the CVE exploitable in our runtime config? if not exploitable maybe we can do a temporary policy exception with compensating controls.

security-oncall: I pulled the SBOM and did a quick triage — package "fastyaml" v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4 contains CVE-2025-1234 (path traversal). In our config the feature that exposes the path parsing is disabled by default, but runtime still links the vulnerable symbol. Recommend either pin to the previous digest or apply a rebuild that drops the vulnerable wheel.

qa: regression suite on canary passed before this, but we didn't run the specific fuzzer for yaml parsing in CI for this release. I can kick off the fuzzer on a dev cluster now.

release-manager: options list so we can decide quickly: 1) pin artifact to last known-good digest and proceed in change window, 2) rebuild artifact with fastyaml pinned to 2.1.2 and rerun scans, 3) request an emergency compliance exception for today with mitigation, 4) rollback the release entirely. What are timelines for each?

alex: pin -> ~15min (if we already have the digest in the registry), rebuild -> ~45-90min + scans, exception -> depends on legal/compliance but usually 2-4h to review, rollback -> quick but will block the feature.

irene: compliance exception is last resort. If pin is feasible and we have LKG digest, that's the fastest safe path. Security-oncall, can you confirm LKG digest exists and matches the previously scanned SBOM?

security-oncall: confirmed — registry has digest sha256:aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66aa77bb88cc99ddeeff00112233445566778899aa from 2025-03-12 09:21 UTC. That digest passed vuln-scan and integrity checks. We can pin to that digest.

maria: good. does pinning affect other downstream images or shards? any risk of mismatch with migrations we bundled?

alex: we've validated migration scripts are content-addressed and not dependent on the wheel version. Downstream services should be fine. Need to update release notes to mark this as pin and include the reason.

qa: I'll run fuzzer and smoke again against the pinned digest once it's pushed to the canary tag. ETA ~20min.

release-manager: decision: pin to LKG digest, unblock canary in the next change window at 14:00 UTC, and run expanded vuln/fuzz tests in staging. If fuzzer finds issues, we'll rollback. Action items: @alex pin artifact and push canary tag, @qa run fuzzer and report in this thread, @irene coordinate a post-deploy validation checklist, @maria update release notes and customer advisory draft.

alex: starting pin now — pushing tag redwood/runtime:canary-0.48.1-pin -> sha256:aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66aa77bb88cc99ddeeff00112233445566778899aa

deploy-bot: Tag push detected. Re-running SBOM and vuln-scan against tag redwood/runtime:canary-0.48.1-pin

deploy-bot: SBOM integrity: OK. vuln-scan: no new findings. Canary deployment scheduled for 2025-03-18 14:00:00 UTC per change window.

qa: fuzzer started on dev-cluster-3, 3h job but I'll post interim progress. so far 0 crashes in first 20 minutes.

irene: I'll prepare the validation checklist (yaml parser smoke, auth boundaries, ingestion rate tests). Will also schedule a quick post-canary call at 15:30 UTC.

maria: release notes updated with "artifact pinned due to SBOM integrity mismatch; reason: introduced medium CVE in transitive dependency; mitigation: pinned to previously scanned digest." Draft customer advisory attached: https://docs.internal/releases/advisories/v0.48.1-digest-pin.md

release-manager: thanks team. keeping thread open until post-canary validation completes. If fuzzer or post-canary validations fail, we revert to rollback plan.

alex: noted. will report back once canary is up. TL;DR: pin to LKG digest, unblock in 14:00 UTC change window, run extra validations, rollback if anything fails. :thumbsup:
